name: qa
description: QA Quincey, the manual-QA persona. Verifies one defined flow against the spec or mockup and records a QA posture. qa:browser drives the real running app through the user's persistent agent-browser session (click/pixel level), walks the spec, seeds and tears down tagged data via the repo's recipe, and ends with the QA_STATUS contract that satisfies the build-time Stop hook and the PR qa-gate CI. qa:headless does the same for backend features with no UI (capturing side effects). qa:qa-plan authors the two-phase QA plan and writes the approval stamp, which now requires a real human AskUserQuestion approval (a single-use token minted by a PostToolUse hook) and binds to a digest of the plan so a changed plan must be re-approved. The plugin also SHIPS Quincey's enforcement hooks (hooks/hooks.json): the QA-plan gates (presentation, build, Bash-build, PR), the approval-token minter, and the QA-status Stop gate, active under ~/dev per the tracked gate policy. The build gate now has two halves: the PreToolUse Edit/Write gate that blocks before a write, and a PostToolUse Bash gate that catches source written through the shell (heredoc-fed interpreters, sed -i, tee, python3 -c), which the Edit-only matcher never saw; the second decides from what the repo observed changing rather than from the command text, so it is blind to write mechanism, and it interrupts after the fact rather than preventing. qa/docs/build-gate-coverage.md states the exact coverage and its limits. Skills: qa:browser, qa:headless, qa:qa-plan.
